title: These clever apps show off the iPhone Duo’s potential

evidence.quote: (The Duo starts at $2,000).

claims.claim: Deck-Man, formerly known as Duo-Man, was designed by indie developer Vidit Bhargava at a hackathon.

evidence.quote: Designed by indie developer Vidit Bhargava at a hackathon, the music player takes clever advantage of the Duo’s two screens to imitate how Walkman cassette players used to function.
I have to credit Deck-Man, which was previously known as Duo-Man, as being the first app that made me want to get a Duo. Designed by indie developer Vidit Bhargava at a hackathon

claims.claim: TypeDraw fonts were designed by its creator, Phil Traut.

evidence.quote: Inside TypeDraw, you can type using a font that’s your own handwriting or pick from one of a dozen fonts designed by its creator, Phil Traut.

claims.claim: Wakeout is a former Apple App of the Year winner.

evidence.quote: Wakeout, the workout app that’s a former Apple App of the Year winner, has also approached its Duo optimization thoughtfully

claims.claim: Tiny Computers features 10 retro computers and has a $3.99 one-time fee with no ads or subscriptions.

evidence.quote: Netflix is one of Apple’s hand-picked partners for the Duo launch, and had its streaming app Duo-optimized by the time the device shipped, alongside others like the MLB app, NYT Cooking, Slack, my preferred calendar app Fantastical, and others.

claims.claim: Flighty is an Apple Design Award-winning travel app.

evidence.quote: Already my favorite travel app, Apple Design Award-winning Flighty tells you everything you need to know about your upcoming flight
